paragraph: Fort Lee's single-family tier is small, 23 sales over six months at a median of $1,108,800, with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.02 and 61 percent of homes closing above asking. Median days on market of 30 keeps this competitive rather than frenzied. Condos and townhouses carry the volume with 145 sales at a median of $600,000, and this category includes new-construction side-by-side duplexes built on torn-down single-family lots, not only high-rise units. Buckingham, Atrium Palace, and The Palisades trade regularly. Co-ops sit at the entry point, 87 sales at a median of $236,000, with a 55-day median days on market that tells you sellers there are okay with waiting for the right buyer. Horizon House, The Plaza, and Century Tower are the names to know, and they come with board approval, financing restrictions, and resale friction, which not every buyer is aware of going in. Look into the specifics before you fall in love with a unit. On the seasonal read, condo volume held steady all six months while the median swung from $649,500 in April to $490,000 in July, which points to a mix shift toward smaller units rather than falling values. Single-family months are too thin to read on their own. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo, or the lower price point of a co-op.
